title: Terraform from First Principles: Read, Plan & Build the Stack
subtitle: Learn HCL and state, then deploy a connected infrastructure lab with a deliberate image/migration bootstrap.
analogy: Terraform is a planner with a ledger. HCL describes the desired infrastructure; state records which remote objects it manages. The plan compares configuration, recorded addresses and observed cloud objects before proposing changes.
objectives: Read resource blocks, references, expressions, variables and outputs.
Explain state, dependency graphs, drift, replacement and provider lockfiles.
Build the network, data, identity, container and scaling layers in the right order.
Inspect a saved plan, deploy an immutable image, migrate, and verify the complete result.
prerequisites: The local application passes tests and you understand Chapters 3–7.
Terraform 1.11+ and AWS CLI v2 are installed; SSO is authenticated to the intended account.
This is a new bootcamp-iac stack. Manually created resources from earlier exercises are not automatically imported; clean them up separately or budget for both stacks.

lessons.title: Read HCL instead of memorizing resource names
body: A `resource` block manages a remote object. Its two labels identify its type and local name, for example aws_vpc.main. Arguments configure it. A `data` block reads an existing value, such as AWS’s ECS AMI parameter. An `output` exposes a result for a person or another tool.

`var.project_name` reads an input; `local.roles` reads a reusable expression. `count` creates indexed instances, while `for_each` creates instances keyed by stable strings. `aws_subnet.private[*].id` collects all private subnet IDs. `jsonencode` converts structured HCL into the JSON expected by ECS or IAM.

lessons.title: Dependencies come from values, not filenames
body: Terraform loads all .tf files in a directory as one module. Numeric file prefixes help humans read; they do not control creation order. A subnet referencing aws_vpc.main.id depends on the VPC regardless of file names.

Use depends_on only for dependencies not already represented by a value. The API service references its target group but also waits for the listener and startup policies, because those readiness requirements are not fully represented by the task-definition ARN.

lessons.title: State and two kinds of lockfile
body: State maps resource addresses to cloud IDs; never commit it or treat it as a harmless cache. Sensitive output flags redact display but do not remove values from state. This lab avoids reading the generated RDS password into state.

`.terraform.lock.hcl` records provider selections and checksums; commit it. The S3 `.tflock` object coordinates concurrent state writers; do not commit or manually delete it. These are different from uv.lock, which resolves Python packages.

lessons.title: What init, plan and apply actually do
body: init installs providers and configures a backend. fmt formats HCL. validate checks structure and provider schemas without provisioning. plan refreshes observed state by default and proposes a diff. apply executes the reviewed plan; it can fail partially, leaving successfully created resources recorded in state.

Read create (+), update (~), destroy (-) and replacement (-/+) carefully. Creating a database takes real time and may incur charges; neither a fixed seven-minute deployment nor automatic typo prevention is guaranteed. A valid configuration is not proof of account permissions, quotas or regional engine availability.

lessons.title: Bootstrap the application in phases
body: Copy only 00-versions.tf through 06-ec2.tf and outputs.tf for this chapter. enable_services=false creates foundations and task definitions without trying to pull an unpublished image. It also leaves the optional EC2 group at zero hosts.

First provision foundations. Then publish the image, persist its tag in a local ignored auto.tfvars file, update task definitions, run the one-off migration and check its exit code. Only then enable the services. Subsequent releases must preserve these inputs; a missing enable_services flag would plan to remove the services.

lessons.title: Understand the lab tradeoffs
body: The baseline has two public/private subnets, one NAT, a private single-instance database and a single TLS cache node. The API uses Fargate; the worker can use Fargate or optionally an EC2 capacity provider.

Deletion protection and final snapshots are disabled only for the disposable lab. Production needs HTTPS/authentication, restricted DB users, verified TLS, cache ACLs/failover, backup/restore tests and a reviewed access policy. A plan may reveal infrastructure changes as well as a new app image.

handHoldingSteps: Create infra/ and copy the complete runnable file set below, excluding hcl-fundamentals.tf.txt and the optional backend example. Do not paste reading fragments as extra resources.
Authenticate with SSO. Run init, fmt and validate. Commit .terraform.lock.hcl. Use the foundations plan to inspect costs and resource changes before apply.

Build and push the image to the Terraform-created ECR URL. Save image_tag and enable_services=false to infra/release.auto.tfvars; that file is intentionally ignored and contains settings, not credentials.

Apply the image-only configuration update so the API task definition points to the pushed tag. Run the migration command, wait for the task to stop and confirm exit code 0. If it fails, inspect stoppedReason/container reason and logs before proceeding.
Change enable_services to true in release.auto.tfvars. Plan and apply again, wait for stable services and test the ALB business path. Keep this settings file for later plan/destroy commands.

Optionally set worker_on_ec2=true in the same settings file and review the plan: it replaces the worker service location and starts host capacity. This creates a processing transition; schedule it deliberately.

Before collaborating or using a Terraform pipeline, provision a separate private/versioned state bucket, copy backend.tf.example to backend.tf and migrate state. Do not place the backend bucket under this application stack’s destroy lifecycle.
concepts: Declarative desired state: Terraform chooses an execution graph; line order is not a shell script.
Implicit reference: Reading another resource’s attribute creates a dependency automatically.
State ownership: Changing HCL does not automatically adopt console-created objects; import is a deliberate mapping operation.
Drift: Plan can show out-of-band changes, but only for attributes managed/read by the provider; it is not a universal cloud security audit.
Lifecycle boundaries: Terraform manages service configuration; Application Auto Scaling owns API desired_count after registration.

commands.command:
aws sts get-caller-identity
terraform -chdir=infra init
terraform -chdir=infra fmt -check
terraform -chdir=infra validate
git add infra/.terraform.lock.hcl
commands.explanation: Verify identity and initialize the provider. No AWS resources are created by init/validate.
commands.expected: Valid HCL/provider schema; provider lockfile staged for review.

commands.command:
terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=foundations.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra show foundations.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra apply foundations.tfplan
commands.explanation: The default enable_services=false provisions foundations only. Review the plan before running apply. Saved plans may contain sensitive information; keep them out of Git.
commands.expected: Network, data, ECR, roles and task definitions exist; no API/worker service runs yet.

commands.command:
ECR_URL=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw ecr_url)
IMAGE_TAG=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
REGISTRY="${ECR_URL%%/*}"
aws ecr get-login-password --region "$AWS_REGION" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG" .
docker push "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG"
printf 'image_tag = "%s"\nenable_services = false\nworker_on_ec2 = false\n' "$IMAGE_TAG" > infra/release.auto.tfvars
terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=image.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra apply image.tfplan
commands.explanation: Commit source before selecting the SHA. Persist release inputs so later plans do not fall back to bootstrap/disabled defaults.
commands.expected: Both task-definition families reference the published image.

commands.command:
run_migration() {
  CLUSTER=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw cluster_name) || return
  TASK_DEF=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw migration_task_definition) || return
  NETWORK=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw migration_network) || return
  MIGRATION_TASK=$(aws ecs run-task --cluster "$CLUSTER" --launch-type FARGATE \
    --task-definition "$TASK_DEF" --network-configuration "$NETWORK" \
    --overrides '{"containerOverrides":[{"name":"api","command":["alembic","upgrade","head"]}]}' \
    --query 'tasks[0].taskArn' --output text) || return
  test "$MIGRATION_TASK" != None || return 1
  aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster "$CLUSTER" --tasks "$MIGRATION_TASK" || return
  EXIT_CODE=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "$CLUSTER" --tasks "$MIGRATION_TASK" --query 'tasks[0].containers[0].exitCode' --output text) || return
  test "$EXIT_CODE" = 0
}
run_migration
commands.explanation: Run inside the private network using the task definition’s secret/settings. If run-task returns failures, do not continue; inspect its response and CloudWatch logs. The function returns immediately on an AWS/CLI failure; do not enable services unless it returns success.
commands.expected: The one-off migration exits 0 before services are enabled.

commands.command:
# Edit release.auto.tfvars: keep image_tag and set enable_services = true.
terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=services.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra apply services.tfplan
aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$CLUSTER" --services bootcamp-iac-api bootcamp-iac-worker
BASE_URL=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw alb_url)
curl --fail "$BASE_URL/ready"
curl -i -X POST "$BASE_URL/enqueue" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello Terraform"}'
sleep 3
curl --fail "$BASE_URL/jobs"
commands.explanation: Apply the reviewed service plan, then verify the real request-to-result path. If worker_on_ec2=true, wait for bootcamp-iac-worker-ec2 instead.
commands.expected: Healthy targets and a completed database result.

commands.command:
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket YOUR_GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_STATE_BUCKET --region us-east-1
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket YOUR_GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_STATE_BUCKET --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket YOUR_GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_STATE_BUCKET --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
cp infra/backend.tf.example infra/backend.tf
terraform -chdir=infra init -migrate-state -backend-config="bucket=YOUR_GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_STATE_BUCKET" -backend-config="region=us-east-1"
commands.explanation: Optional collaboration setup, using a separate bucket. Replace the bucket name; the create-bucket syntax shown is for us-east-1. Preserve the state migration backup securely. Backend access needs state object read/write and lock-object read/write/delete permissions.
commands.expected: State migrates to private versioned S3 with native use_lockfile locking; no DynamoDB table is required.

codeFiles.description: Read HCL structure before copying the complete file set below.

walkthrough.title: Block type and labels
walkthrough.explanation: resource is the block type; aws_vpc is the provider resource type; main is your local label. Together aws_vpc.main is an address, not the AWS display name.

walkthrough.title: Arguments and values
walkthrough.explanation: cidr_block is an argument assigned a string. Booleans use true/false without quotes; lists use brackets and maps use braces.

walkthrough.title: References
walkthrough.explanation: aws_vpc.main.id reads an attribute of another resource. Terraform records that dependency; it is not a shell variable.

walkthrough.title: Variables, locals, data and outputs
walkthrough.explanation: Variables are inputs, locals name expressions, data sources read existing information, resources manage lifecycle, and outputs expose selected results.

codeFiles.description: Provider constraints, region, typed inputs and explicit disabled-service bootstrap.
The complete two-AZ network and security-group path.

walkthrough.title: aws_vpc.main
walkthrough.explanation: Creates an isolated address space. Referencing its ID makes dependent network resources wait for the VPC.

walkthrough.title: aws_internet_gateway.main
walkthrough.explanation: Connects a public route table to the internet. Attaching it does not expose private tasks by itself.

walkthrough.title: aws_subnet.public
walkthrough.explanation: Slices the VPC CIDR and places each subnet into one AZ. count.index selects a distinct subnet and zone.

walkthrough.title: aws_subnet.private
walkthrough.explanation: Slices the VPC CIDR and places each subnet into one AZ. count.index selects a distinct subnet and zone.

walkthrough.title: aws_eip.nat
walkthrough.explanation: Allocates the public IPv4 address used by NAT; it can incur charges independently of running application tasks.

walkthrough.title: aws_nat_gateway.main
walkthrough.explanation: Enables outbound IPv4 traffic from private subnets. This lab uses one gateway, with an AZ/cost tradeoff.

walkthrough.title: aws_route_table.public
walkthrough.explanation: Defines the default next hop. The public table uses the internet gateway; the private table uses NAT.

walkthrough.title: aws_route_table.private
walkthrough.explanation: Defines the default next hop. The public table uses the internet gateway; the private table uses NAT.

walkthrough.title: aws_route_table_association.public
walkthrough.explanation: Actually connects a subnet to its route table. A correct unassociated table would have no effect.

walkthrough.title: aws_route_table_association.private
walkthrough.explanation: Actually connects a subnet to its route table. A correct unassociated table would have no effect.

walkthrough.title: aws_security_group.alb
walkthrough.explanation: Defines stateful allowed connections. alb accepts public HTTP, app accepts 8000 from alb, and data accepts DB/cache ports only from app.

walkthrough.title: aws_security_group.app
walkthrough.explanation: Defines stateful allowed connections. alb accepts public HTTP, app accepts 8000 from alb, and data accepts DB/cache ports only from app.

walkthrough.title: aws_security_group.data
walkthrough.explanation: Defines stateful allowed connections. alb accepts public HTTP, app accepts 8000 from alb, and data accepts DB/cache ports only from app.

codeFiles.code:
resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "main" {
  name       = "${var.project_name}-db"
  subnet_ids = aws_subnet.private[*].id
}
resource "aws_db_instance" "postgres" {
  identifier                  = "${var.project_name}-postgres"
  engine                      = "postgres"
  engine_version              = "17"
  instance_class              = "db.t4g.micro"
  allocated_storage           = 20
  storage_encrypted           = true
  db_name                     = "appdb"
  username                    = "appuser"
  manage_master_user_password = true
  db_subnet_group_name        = aws_db_subnet_group.main.name
  vpc_security_group_ids      = [aws_security_group.data.id]
  publicly_accessible         = false
  backup_retention_period     = 1
  # Disposable lab only: take a final snapshot for data you need to keep.
  skip_final_snapshot = true
  deletion_protection = false
}
resource "aws_elasticache_subnet_group" "main" {
  name       = "${var.project_name}-cache"
  subnet_ids = aws_subnet.private[*].id
}
resource "aws_elasticache_replication_group" "queue" {
  replication_group_id       = "${var.project_name}-queue"
  description                = "Private TaskIQ stream broker for the lab"
  engine                     = "valkey"
  engine_version             = "7.2"
  node_type                  = "cache.t4g.micro"
  num_cache_clusters         = 1
  automatic_failover_enabled = false
  subnet_group_name          = aws_elasticache_subnet_group.main.name
  security_group_ids         = [aws_security_group.data.id]
  at_rest_encryption_enabled = true
  transit_encryption_enabled = true
}
# RDS generates the password in Secrets Manager; Terraform reads only its ARN.
# This lab uses the DB owner for brevity. Real apps need a restricted SQL role.
# The single cache node has no failover. Add replicas and ACL/auth for production.
codeFiles.description: Private PostgreSQL with a managed password and a TLS Valkey endpoint.

walkthrough.title: aws_db_subnet_group.main
walkthrough.explanation: Supplies private subnets across AZs where RDS is permitted to create database network interfaces.

walkthrough.title: aws_db_instance.postgres
walkthrough.explanation: Creates PostgreSQL 17 with encryption and no public address. RDS generates its password in Secrets Manager; Terraform retains a reference to the secret, not its generated value.

walkthrough.title: aws_elasticache_subnet_group.main
walkthrough.explanation: Constrains cache placement to private subnets.

walkthrough.title: aws_elasticache_replication_group.queue
walkthrough.explanation: Creates the Redis-compatible Valkey endpoint. TLS and at-rest encryption are enabled; one node deliberately omits failover for this lab.

codeFiles.description: Trust and permissions for ECS execution and task identities.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role.execution
walkthrough.explanation: Defines an identity and its trust policy: who may assume it. Permissions come from attached policies, not from the role name.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.execution
walkthrough.explanation: Attaches a managed policy to an identity. Execution and host policies grant different service permissions.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role_policy.db_secret
walkthrough.explanation: Adds scoped inline permissions. Secret retrieval belongs to the execution role; ECS Exec channel access belongs to the task role.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role.task
walkthrough.explanation: Defines an identity and its trust policy: who may assume it. Permissions come from attached policies, not from the role name.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role_policy.exec
walkthrough.explanation: Adds scoped inline permissions. Secret retrieval belongs to the execution role; ECS Exec channel access belongs to the task role.

codeFiles.description: ECR, logs, cluster, ALB, shared container settings, task definitions and gated services.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecr_repository.app
walkthrough.explanation: Stores release images. Immutable tags prevent accidentally overwriting a commit’s published image. force_delete is a destructive lab teardown choice.

walkthrough.title: aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app
walkthrough.explanation: Creates a destination and retention period for container logs. A named log group does not itself create logs; the task definition must use awslogs.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_cluster.main
walkthrough.explanation: Creates the scheduling/control-plane grouping. A cluster alone does not start a container or create an EC2 host.

walkthrough.title: aws_lb.main
walkthrough.explanation: Creates the public application load balancer in the public subnet pair.

walkthrough.title: aws_lb_target_group.api
walkthrough.explanation: Defines IP targets on port 8000 and /ready health checks. ECS registers and deregisters task IPs as deployments change.

walkthrough.title: aws_lb_listener.http
walkthrough.explanation: Accepts HTTP on port 80 and forwards to the API target group. Production TLS needs a separate HTTPS listener and ACM certificate.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_task_definition.app
walkthrough.explanation: Registers launch configuration: shared image tag, command, environment, secret references, roles, resources and logs. for_each creates API and worker families from one definition pattern.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_service.api
walkthrough.explanation: Maintains running replicas from a task-definition revision. enable_services gates creation until the image and schema exist. Only the API attaches to ALB.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_service.worker
walkthrough.explanation: Maintains running replicas from a task-definition revision. enable_services gates creation until the image and schema exist. Only the API attaches to ALB.

codeFiles.description: API service autoscaling with Terraform desired_count ownership handled explicitly.

walkthrough.title: aws_appautoscaling_target.api
walkthrough.explanation: Registers service desired count with bounds. The API resource ID uses the actual cluster and service names.

walkthrough.title: aws_appautoscaling_policy.api_cpu
walkthrough.explanation: Adds CPU target tracking and asymmetric cooldowns. It does not add queue-backlog scaling or guarantee a response time.

codeFiles.description: Optional EC2 worker capacity. The default creates no running EC2 hosts.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role.host
walkthrough.explanation: Defines an identity and its trust policy: who may assume it. Permissions come from attached policies, not from the role name.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.host
walkthrough.explanation: Attaches a managed policy to an identity. Execution and host policies grant different service permissions.

walkthrough.title: aws_iam_instance_profile.host
walkthrough.explanation: Associates a host IAM role with EC2. This is not the application task role.

walkthrough.title: aws_launch_template.host
walkthrough.explanation: Defines the host AMI, machine size, instance profile, IMDSv2 setting and cluster-registration user data.

walkthrough.title: aws_autoscaling_group.host
walkthrough.explanation: Supplies EC2 hosts in private subnets. worker_on_ec2=false gives a zero-host lab baseline; managed scaling may later change desired_capacity.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_capacity_provider.ec2
walkthrough.explanation: Connects ECS task demand to an ASG. target_capacity=80 is a reservation target, not a guaranteed memory percentage.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_providers.main
walkthrough.explanation: Registers Fargate and the optional EC2 provider with this cluster before EC2 services use it.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_task_definition.worker_ec2
walkthrough.explanation: Registers launch configuration: shared image tag, command, environment, secret references, roles, resources and logs. for_each creates API and worker families from one definition pattern.

walkthrough.title: aws_ecs_service.worker_ec2
walkthrough.explanation: Maintains running replicas from a task-definition revision. enable_services gates creation until the image and schema exist. Only the API attaches to ALB.

codeFiles.description: Non-secret outputs used by the deployment commands.

walkthrough.title: -raw outputs
walkthrough.explanation: These strings let shell commands use actual ARNs, network configuration and endpoints rather than copying IDs from screenshots.

codeFiles.description: Optional S3 backend. The bucket must exist outside this module before activating this file.

walkthrough.title: use_lockfile
walkthrough.explanation: Opt into S3-native locking. Bucket versioning supports recovery; backend IAM protects who can read state and acquire/delete the lock.

flowDescription: Validate + plan → Apply foundations → Publish image → Update definitions → Run migration → Enable + verify.

breakItDrill.title: Detect managed drift safely
breakItDrill.scenario: In the lab console, change the managed CloudWatch log retention from 7 to 14 days, then run terraform plan.
breakItDrill.symptom: The plan proposes restoring the configured retention. Unlike adding an SSH rule, this drill does not open public access.
breakItDrill.fix: Review and apply the reconciliation, or change HCL deliberately if the new retention is intended.

assignment.title: Explain and deploy the stack
assignment.description: For each Terraform file, describe the AWS objects it creates, the inputs it consumes and the outputs/references that create dependencies. Deploy the baseline and optionally move the worker to EC2. Include migration output and a completed job ID in your notes.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: Understand the plan and its dependency graph before applying it; state is the ledger of ownership.
bullets: Copy the full file set; numeric names do not define execution order.
Persist image_tag and enable_services inputs across releases.
A generated password can stay in Secrets Manager without its plaintext entering state.
Review every replacement and destroy operation.

checklist.text: Read resource blocks, references, expressions, variables and outputs.
Explain state, dependency graphs, drift, replacement and provider lockfiles.
Build the network, data, identity, container and scaling layers in the right order.
Inspect a saved plan, deploy an immutable image, migrate, and verify the complete result.
